subject: Cloud Computing
title: Showback and Chargeback
description: Learn Showback and Chargeback in one minute.

hook.text: The company's cloud bill is $500,000/month. But nobody knows which team is spending what. Sound familiar?

buildup.text: Showback reports costs by team without billing them. Chargeback actually charges each team's budget.

discovery.text: Both rely on tagging resources with team names, projects, and environments. Without tags, cost attribution is guesswork.

twist.text: Shared services — like databases used by five teams — make cost allocation messy. Who pays for the shared portion?

climax.text: When teams see their own costs, behavior changes overnight. Accountability drives efficiency.

punchline.text: Show teams their cloud bill. Watch spending drop instantly.

quiz.question: What is the difference between showback and chargeback?
options: Showback reports costs for visibility; chargeback bills teams from their budgets
Showback is for small companies; chargeback is for enterprises only
Showback uses monthly billing; chargeback uses annual billing

details.summary: Showback displays cloud costs to each team without billing them directly. Chargeback actually charges costs to each team's budget. Both use cost allocation tags to attribute spending. These practices create accountability by making teams see the financial impact of their decisions.
details.whyItMatters: When teams do not see their cloud costs, they have no incentive to optimize. Showback and chargeback create the feedback loop needed for responsible cloud spending.
takeaways: Showback shows costs; chargeback bills costs to each team
Cost allocation tags attribute spending to teams and projects
Creates accountability and incentives for cost optimization

faq.question: What is the difference between showback and chargeback?
faq.answer: Showback provides visibility by reporting each team's costs without financial consequences. Chargeback actually bills costs to each team's department budget. Showback is easier to implement and creates awareness, while chargeback creates stronger financial accountability.

faq.question: How do you implement cost allocation tags?
faq.answer: Define a mandatory tagging policy with tags for team, project, environment, and cost center. Enforce tagging through cloud policies that prevent creating untagged resources. Audit tag compliance regularly. Use tag-based cost reports for showback or chargeback.
